questions.text:
f(x) = 4x³ – 7x² + 2x/3 + 5.

Use calculus to find the gradient of f(x) at x = –1.
For f(x) = x³/3 – x² + 4x – 2, find the equation of the tangent to the curve at x = 3.
questions.markingGuide: f'(x) = x² – 2x + 4. f'(3) = 9 – 6 + 4 = 7 (gradient of tangent). f(3) = 27/3 – 9 + 12 – 2 = 9 – 9 + 12 – 2 = 10. Tangent: y – 10 = 7(x – 3), so y = 7x – 21 + 10 = 7x – 11. Merit = correct tangent equation with full working.

questions.text:
The gradient function is f'(x) = 3x² – 6x – 24.

Find f(x) given that the y-value of the local minimum is –48.
questions.markingGuide: Antidifferentiate: f(x) = x³ – 3x² – 24x + c. Stationary points: f'(x) = 3x² – 6x – 24 = 3(x² – 2x – 8) = 3(x – 4)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 4 or x = –2. f''(x) = 6x – 6. f''(4) = 18 > 0 so x = 4 is a local minimum. f(4) = 64 – 48 – 96 + c = –80 + c. Set = –48: c = 32. Therefore f(x) = x³ – 3x² – 24x + 32. Excellence = correct full working including constant.

questions.text:
A bus moves at a constant speed of 5 m/s past a stop. A car, starting from rest at the bus stop, accelerates at 0.5 m/s² to catch the bus.

At the moment the car leaves, the bus is 200 m ahead.

Find the distance from the bus stop when the car catches the bus.
questions.expectedAnswer: 400 m from bus stop (at t = 40 s)
questions.markingGuide: Let t = time after car starts. Bus position: s_B(t) = 5t + 200 (head start of 200 m). Car velocity: v(t) = 0.5t. Integrate: s_C(t) = 0.25t². They meet when s_C = s_B: 0.25t² = 5t + 200, i.e. t² – 20t – 800 = 0. Factorise: (t – 40)(t + 20) = 0. Since t > 0, t = 40 s. Distance: s_C(40) = 0.25 × 1600 = 400 m. Check: bus = 5(40) + 200 = 400 m ✓. Achieved = integration. Merit = correct equation. Excellence = complete solution.

questions.text:
The graph of f(x) is a positive cubic (rises left to right) with two turning points.

Sketch f'(x).
questions.expectedAnswer: Upward-opening parabola with x-intercepts at the turning points of f(x)
questions.markingGuide: f'(x) is quadratic, opens upward, zeros at the turning points of f(x). Achieved = 2 of 3 features. Merit = all 3.

questions.text:
f'(x) = 4x³ – 3x² + 2x + 5.

The graph of f(x) passes through (1, 4). Find f(x).

The temperature of a cooling loaf of bread is modelled by:

T(t) = t²/20 – 3t + 60

where T is °C and t is minutes.

Show that the rate of change of temperature is –1 °C/min when t = 20.
The cooling loaf was taken out of the oven. Use calculus to determine at what time the loaf cools most rapidly (reaches minimum temperature rate of change).
questions.expectedAnswer: The loaf cools most rapidly at t = 0 (rate of change is –3 °C/min, the most negative value since T'(t) is strictly increasing).
questions.markingGuide: T'(t) = t/10 – 3. T''(t) = 1/10 = 0.1 > 0 for all t, so T'(t) is strictly increasing. The minimum (most negative) rate of change therefore occurs at the earliest time, t = 0, where T'(0) = –3 °C/min. So the loaf cools most rapidly at the instant it is taken out of the oven. Excellence = correct reasoning using second derivative and boundary argument.

questions.text:
f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + 5.

f(1) = 0 and f'(–1) = 0. Also a = –1.

Use calculus to find the x-coordinate of the other stationary point.
questions.markingGuide: a = –1, so f(x) = –x³ + bx² + cx + 5. f(1) = –1 + b + c + 5 = 0 → b + c = –4 …(1). f'(x) = –3x² + 2bx + c. f'(–1) = –3 – 2b + c = 0 …(2). From (1): c = –4 – b. Substitute into (2): –3 – 2b + (–4 – b) = 0 → –7 – 3b = 0 → b = –7/3, and c = –4 + 7/3 = –5/3. So f'(x) = –3x² – (14/3)x – 5/3. Set f'(x) = 0 and multiply by –3: 9x² + 14x + 5 = 0 → (9x + 5)(x + 1) = 0. So x = –1 (the given stationary point) or x = –5/9. The other stationary point is at x = –5/9.

questions.text: Determine the nature of the stationary point found in (d)(i) using calculus.
questions.markingGuide: f''(x) = –6x + 2b = –6x – 14/3. At x = –5/9: f''(–5/9) = –6(–5/9) – 14/3 = 30/9 – 14/3 = 10/3 – 14/3 = –4/3 < 0. Since f''(–5/9) < 0, the stationary point at x = –5/9 is a local maximum. Excellence = correct second derivative, evaluated, with conclusion.

questions.text:
f(x) = 2x² – 8x – 5.

Find the point on the curve where the gradient equals 4.

A rectangle's area is expanding such that its length is always 4 times its width.

Find the rate of change of area with respect to width when the area equals 100 cm².
questions.markingGuide: Width = w, length = 4w. A = 4w². A'(w) = 8w. When A = 100: 4w² = 100, w = 5. A'(5) = 40.

questions.text: A lidless rectangular container has width three times its height. Maximum material is 6.4 m². Use calculus to find the maximum volume and prove it's a maximum.
questions.markingGuide: Let height = h, width = 3h, length = L. Lidless surface area = base + 4 walls = 3hL + 2(3h·h) + 2(L·h) = 5hL + 6h² = 6.4, so L = (6.4 – 6h²)/(5h). Volume V = 3h²L = 3h²(6.4 – 6h²)/(5h) = (3h/5)(6.4 – 6h²) = (19.2h – 18h³)/5. dV/dh = (19.2 – 54h²)/5 = 0, so h² = 19.2/54 = 16/45 and h = 4/(3√5) ≈ 0.5963 m. Then L ≈ 1.431 m. V ≈ (19.2(0.5963) – 18(0.5963)³)/5 ≈ (11.449 – 3.816)/5 ≈ 1.527 m³. Confirm maximum: d²V/dh² = –108h/5 < 0 for h > 0. Excellence = correct maximum volume with proof.

questions.text:
f(x) = x⁴/4 + (n – 3)x³/3 – 3nx²/2 + n.

Determine where f(x) is decreasing.
questions.expectedAnswer: f(x) is decreasing for x < –n and 0 < x < 3
questions.markingGuide: f'(x) = x³ + (n–3)x² – 3nx = x[x² + (n–3)x – 3n] = x(x–3)(x+n). Stationary points at x = 0, 3, –n. For n > 0, order: –n, 0, 3. Sign analysis: f(x) decreasing when f'(x) < 0, i.e. x < –n and 0 < x < 3. Achieved = correct derivative. Merit = stationary points found. Excellence = correct decreasing regions.
